questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A general curiosity about a different culture and political landscape. Coming from Denmark, it's always crucial to take new and exciting opportunities, and to have a chance to go to one of the biggest countries in the world was hard to pass on.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university was really great in providing information and checklists to complete upon arrival. Also they provided a community (in the beginning) for new international students, so that everybody had a place to go to and events to participate in.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The checklist, as mentioned before, ensured that all the individual documents, assignments, and so on were completed, to be able to study in the country. Also, they had an office whose task was to assist the international students, so if you needed anything, they had a place for you to seek the information needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit hard, but it also depends on the price you are willing to pay for a rental. But its important to sign up for all the housing rental sites on Facebook, where pretty much everything thats available will be posted.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: As long as you keep yourself inside bus, cycling, or walking distance, it's a great alternative to the slightly more expensive on-campus housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the university's website, a list of all available courses is provided. The courses you then want to take, you need to search for in a portal called "Cource Search & Enroll". Then in some cases, you need to have an approval to take the cource, and for that, there is a separate portal where you can fill out your credentials to take the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write the listed professor on the cource, or the service email provided in the portal "Cource Search & Enroll".

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all but one of the classes I wanted, because the course was full, and I needed an approval to take the course, which was delayed in the beginning

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Begin early to find the courses you want to take, so that you have time to acquire the necessary approvals.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In the beginning, the courses felt kind of easy, but the deeper we got into the semester, the harder and higher the level of material and task became in the cource, which was a good thing.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of the lectures were quite comparable in the sense that they were interactive classes. Where others were just a professor teaching in front of a big class, without the same level of interactiveness with the students. What surprised me a bit was the number of assignments there were for each cource, where the grade you got for an assignment counted towards your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AAE 422 - Food Systems & Supply Chains
Finance 410 - Bank Management 
REAL EST 306 - Real Estate Process
REAL EST 410 - Real Estate Finance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The University of Wisconsin-Madison is the leading university in regard to real estate in the US, so I would highly recommend those two. For Bank Management, it only relates to the American banking industry, but I would say the theories are still transferable to other banking industries.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a lot of opportunities for sport, free fitness for students, and the opportunity to participate in student tournaments in all kinds of sports like European football, volleyball, basketball, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: all of the above

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take road trips in the state of Wisconsin, but also the states surrounding like Minnesota and Illinois. Take a trip to Chicago as well; it's a really great city. Or, just enjoy the city of Madison, as it also has a lot to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, just be curious and open-minded, then everything is going to be great.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take part in the events provided by the university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not challenging, but politics is a topic not really discussed, especially with people from different sides of the political system. However, it's easier and more acceptable for you as a foringer to ask questions and to be curious about it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The general take on how to interact with other people, they are really open and willing to take you in.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Come prepared, enjoy, and participate in everything you have time for. Also, I hear that their bars a great and cheap.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, everything above provides all the information you need.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To graduate and get a broader cultural understanding and experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Before arriving, in regards to the visa process.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
